title: Frequency of Methods of Local Invasion of Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma
brief_summary: Pancreatic cancer often spreads through local invasion into local structures, including fat, blood vessels, nerves, and nearby organs (stomach, duodenum, spleen, bile duct). Local microscopic invasion is associated with recurrence of pancreatic cancer after pancreatic resection, such that even if the original cancer is surgically removed, microscopic areas of cancer often remain. Data on the patterns of local invasion by pancreatic cancer have not been published. In this study, The investigators hope to investigate the frequency of the various methods of local invasion of pancreatic adenocarcinoma. This would help the investigators better understand how pancreatic cancer spreads, and determine what cancers are not resectable.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Tissue confirmed diagnosis of pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
* Underwent surgical resection for adenocarcinoma at the Columbia University Medical Center between 2001-2009.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Did not undergo surgery.
study_population: Study population will include patients who have been diagnosed with pancreatic adenocarcinoma and who are undergoing surgical resection at CUMC.
